import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    # Extract the source dataframe
    df = inputs["meter_reads"].copy()
    
    # Step 1: Sort by meter_id ASC, read_ts ASC, read_seq ASC
    df = df.sort_values(
        by=["meter_id", "read_ts", "read_seq"],
        ascending=[True, True, True],
        na_position="last"
    )
    
    # Step 2: Dedup - keep LAST row per meter_id
    # After sorting, groupby meter_id and take the last row in each group
    df = df.groupby("meter_id", as_index=False, dropna=False).last()
    
    # Step 3: Aggregate - group by zone (treating NULL as a real group)
    # Use dropna=False to preserve NULL zone as a separate group
    agg_dict = {
        "kwh": "sum",
        "meter_id": "count"  # COUNT(*)
    }
    
    grouped = df.groupby("zone", as_index=False, dropna=False).agg({
        "kwh": "sum",
        "meter_id": "count"
    })
    
    # Rename columns to match output schema
    grouped.columns = ["zone", "total_kwh", "meter_count"]
    
    # Ensure correct column order and types
    result = grouped[["zone", "total_kwh", "meter_count"]]
    
    return {"zone_totals": result}
